extracted.intended_audience: journalists and public relations professionals (and general readers interested in media practice)
extracted.subtask_short: news embargo practices for press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Describes what a news/press embargo is, when and why sources use embargoes (business, medical journals, government), how embargoes are arranged and enforced, and related practices such as lockups and review embargoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a news/press embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: A news embargo or press embargo is a request or requirement by a source that the information or news provided by that source not be published until a certain date or certain conditions have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by businesses (product announcements), medical journals, and government officials; media are given advance knowledge so reports can be prepared to coincide with the announcement date and still meet press time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose — reduce inaccuracy and allow preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: In theory, press embargoes reduce inaccuracy in the reporting of breaking stories by reducing the incentive for journalists to cut corners by writing up information quickly in hopes of 'scooping' the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes give journalists time to research background and prepare more comprehensive, accurate coverage; for medical stories they also allow doctors/scientists to analyze studies before the public sees them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review embargoes for pre-release media (games/hardware/films)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review embargoes are when reviewers are given early access to content or products in exchange for keeping review results secret until the embargo is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes include preventing inaccuracies in reviews, avoiding poor launch sales due to premature negative coverage, and allowing discovered flaws/bugs to be fixed before launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and nature — usually gentlemen's agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes are usually arranged in advance as 'gentlemen's agreements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes publicists send embargoed press releases unsolicited in hopes newsrooms will respect the embargo date without prior agreement; the phrase 'For Immediate Release' indicates information is not embargoed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and consequences for breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the embargo is broken by reporting before then, the source will retaliate by restricting access to further information by that journalist or their publication, giving them a long-term disadvantage relative to more cooperative outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking an embargo is typically considered a serious breach of trust and can result in being barred from advance information; embargoes may be broken accidentally (miscommunication) or intentionally (to scoop competitors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes as one method of influencing media presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: News embargoes are one of several ways a source can influence media presentation of the information they provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related methods include providing information 'on background' or 'not for attribution', limiting/providing 'access', or government/market intervention; how journalists react to such influence implicates journalistic ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lockup procedures for sensitive government announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the release of the budget and other important government announcements, reporters are held in a 'lockup' so that they can prepare stories in advance; they are not permitted to file until after the official announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lockups are aimed at preventing insider trading on the basis of leaked government announcements; examples include IMF biweekly briefings embargoed to a synchronized time and national budget lockups in Canada and Australia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical-journal embargo practice (Ingelfinger rule context)
rubrics_metrics.description: News embargoes are commonly applied on health-related news regarding upcoming medical journal articles; all major medical journals have publication embargoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: JAMA's embargo historically 'holds until 15:00 Central Time on the day before the cover date'; journalists who agree not to publish receive advance copies and, for selected articles, press releases and news-release videos are prepared and released in the week before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated reasons and criticisms for medical-journal embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons given: (1) enable journalists to produce more comprehensive and accurate coverage by allowing time for background research, and (2) enable doctors and scientists to receive and analyze studies before the public does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism: some object that the medical news embargo system is driven by profit motives on the part of journals; scholarly debate and empirical studies (cited) examine whether embargoes serve public interest or journals' status/financial goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between embargoed advance access and unsolicited embargoed releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance copies given to journalists under embargo are typically coordinated with agreement; by contrast, publicists may send embargoed press releases to newsrooms unsolicited hoping they will be respected without prior agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction matters for expectations of enforcement and trust; explicit markers like 'For Immediate Release' clarify a release is not under embargo and should be published immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating types and consequences of embargo handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific historical examples illustrate embargo application and breach consequences (e.g., reporters 'locked up' for government budgets; Piers Morgan intentionally breaching a BBC pay embargo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples serve as practical guidance: intentional breach can provoke public condemnation and professional consequences; lockups and synchronized global embargo times are used to coordinate market-sensitive announcements.
